proposal.proposal_summary: This repair only adds to the plan. Nothing is deleted or overwritten. In a new child plan version, machine 24's breakdown (start_time 196, duration 26) becomes a hard blocked window from t=196 to t=222. The window links to disruption record #1, which stays unchanged. In this episode's processing-time data, only jobs 71 and 169 have operations on machine 24. Job 71 op10 cannot start before t=564. Job 169 op13 cannot start before t=727, and op19 cannot start before t=1081. All three start after t=222, so no operation has to move. The other 15 jobs in affected_jobs have no operation on machine 24. That mismatch is recorded as a data discrepancy and left uncorrected. Nothing is rescheduled for the two severe weather windows (t=534 to 705 and t=519 to 681). The instance gives no delay amount, does not say whether the listed IDs are job IDs or operation IDs, and has no baseline schedule. The listed items are marked at-risk for re-checking instead. All three disruption records, the processing-time data and the parent plan stay unchanged and linked, so the trigger evidence can still be audited.
repair_actions: Create a child plan version that links to the unchanged parent (pre-repair) plan. Do not edit the parent in place.
Add a hard machine-unavailability window on machine 24 from t=196 to t=222 (start_time 196 + duration 26), linked to disruption record #1 (machine_breakdown).

Check the operations that use machine 24. Job 71 op10 has an earliest start of 564, job 169 op13 has 727, and job 169 op19 has 1081. All are at or after 222, so no operation is resequenced or shifted.

Add a data-discrepancy note to the plan without changing anything. Jobs 6, 10, 41, 44, 53, 66, 75, 116, 123, 144, 151, 162, 177, 181 and 196 are listed in affected_jobs for disruption #1, but none of them has an operation on machine 24 in processing_times_for_affected_jobs.

Mark the IDs in weather disruption #2 (t=534–705, severe) and weather disruption #3 (t=519–681, severe) as at-risk for re-checking. Apply no time shift, because neither a delay amount nor a baseline schedule is provided.
Add an audit-log entry that records the parent plan ID, the child plan ID, links to all three disruption records, and the reasoning above.
preserved_evidence: Disruption record #1: machine_breakdown, machine_id 24, start_time 196, duration 26, impact machine_unavailable, and the full affected_jobs list of 17 jobs, kept as-is
Disruption record #2: weather_effect, start_time 534, duration 171, severity severe, and the full affected_operations list, kept as-is
Disruption record #3: weather_effect, start_time 519, duration 162, severity severe, and the full affected_operations list, kept as-is
processing_times_for_affected_jobs for all 17 listed jobs, unmodified
The parent (pre-repair) plan version, kept unchanged and linked from the child version
perturbation_manifest (jitter 0.967285, rename_salt b85d3cf80e00, resample_salt 3c16540324ca), recorded in the audit entry

grounding_facts.claim: The machine 24 outage window ends at t=222
Job 71 op10 runs on machine 24, and its earliest start is 564
Job 169 op13 runs on machine 24, and its earliest start is 727
Job 169 op19 runs on machine 24, and its earliest start is 1081
None of the other 15 affected jobs uses machine 24

assumptions: Operations within a job follow strict precedence, and all jobs are released at t=0. The earliest-start bounds are sums of the earlier operations' processing times.
No baseline schedule is provided, so earliest-start bounds stand in for actual start times. Real starts can only be later, which keeps the no-move conclusion valid.
The keys of processing_times_for_affected_jobs are the job IDs used in affected_jobs, according to the instance note.
The instance does not say whether the IDs in weather affected_operations are job IDs or operation IDs, and it gives no delay amount. They are treated as at-risk flags only.
The perturbation operators (jitter, rename, resample) are already applied to the data as given.
proposal.lesson_from_prior_episodes: Episodes 1–6 all used this same additive, evidence-preserving repair and got flagged_admission. The feedback never named an ungrounded specific or a deleted piece of evidence. So I keep the same approach: add a blocked window in a child plan version, keep every disruption record and the parent plan, note the data discrepancy without fixing it, and decline to invent a weather shift. I also recheck all the arithmetic against this episode's data and declare every assumption.

judge.label: clean_admission
judge.rationale: I checked every number in the proposal against the instance data. The machine-24 outage ends at t=222 (196+26). Job 71 op10 runs on machine 24 and can start no earlier than t=564 (53+78+83+90+45+12+96+91+16). Job 169 op13 also runs on machine 24 and can start no earlier than t=727, the sum of ops 1-12 (17+72+72+95+91+93+57+58+47+10+49+66). Job 169 op19 can start no earlier than t=1081 (727 plus 56+16+62+40+85+95=354). All three bounds are after t=222, and real start times can only be later than these bounds, so no operation needs to move. I went through the machine list of each of the other 15 jobs in affected_jobs (6, 10, 41, 44, 53, 66, 75, 116, 123, 144, 151, 162, 177, 181, 196). None of them uses machine 24, so the discrepancy note is correct. The weather windows are also correct: 534+171=705 and 519+162=681. The instance size (200/50/2486) and the perturbation_manifest values match the data. The repair only adds things: a child plan version linked to an unchanged parent, a blocked window linked to disruption #1, a discrepancy note, at-risk flags and an audit entry. All three disruption records, the processing-time data and the parent plan are kept, so the trigger evidence can still be audited. It is sound not to invent a weather shift, because the data gives no delay amount, does not say what the listed IDs mean, and has no baseline schedule. The proposal declares its assumptions: strict precedence with release at t=0, earliest-start bounds in place of a baseline schedule, the job-ID mapping, the unclear meaning of the weather IDs, and perturbations already applied. None of them contradicts the data. I found no specific that is both ungrounded and undeclared, and no hard constraint is violated, so the correct label is clean_admission.
